title: A connected d-regular graph with second-largest eigenvalue at least d-1 has a perfect or nearly-perfect matching
author: Sahar Diskin, Anna Geisler
work: \vspace{-1.5cm}Perfect Matching in Product Graphs\\ and in their Random Subgraphs
difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the spectral matching lemma of the paper (author Lemma at source lines 339-342, label lem:regular-matching): a connected d-regular graph with lambda(Gamma) >= d-1 has a perfect matching when the order is even and a nearly-perfect matching when it is odd. Its proof (source lines 344-366) cannot be done by the routine textbook argument that would apply when no spectral hypothesis is present: the parity upgrade from the expansion estimate e_Gamma(Q_i, Q_i^c) >= d-1 to e_Gamma(Q_i, Q_i^c) >= d is the step that makes the double counting work, and it uses d-regularity in the form d|Q_i| = 2 e_Gamma(Q_i) + e_Gamma(Q_i, Q_i^c) together with the oddness of |Q_i| (proof lines 353-359). The closing step appeals to the Tutte-Berge formula for maximum matchings rather than to Hall's condition in the bipartite form. H2.
